title: Dyadic Effects of Personality on Sexual Behavior and Experiences in Older Adulthood
abstract: Abstract Sex is a central component of intimate relationships. However, much of our knowledge of the psychological factors shaping satisfying sexual lives is limited to younger adults. We examined individual (i.e., actor) and partner effects of the Big Five personality traits on sexual outcomes (i.e., sexual frequency, sexual and relational quality, and sexual dysfunction) among 953 older opposite-sex couples followed over five years as part of the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project ( M age = 70.60 years, SD = 7.92). Individual and partner conscientiousness were linked to more frequent sex and greater physical and emotional relationship quality, whereas neuroticism was linked to more sexual problems and lower satisfaction. Individual and partner agreeableness were associated with more satisfying sex and relationships. Individual extraversion was positively associated with higher sexual and relational satisfaction and fewer problems, but partner extraversion effects were largely non-significant. Both actor and partner openness were related to poorer evaluations of sex and relationships, but had limited associations with sexual problems. Some gender differences emerged, with more nuanced partner effects for women. Longitudinal analyses indicated that most associations wavered in strength over time. These findings highlight the role of both partners’ personality traits in encouraging sexual and relational well-being in older adulthood.

title: Patterns of Sexual Behavior Initiation Among United States Adolescents
abstract: Abstract Most research on adolescent sexual behavior initiation emphasizes penile–vaginal sex, overlooking other behaviors. We descriptively evaluated initiation patterns of five different sexual behaviors (penetration of the vagina or anus with a finger [fingering], oral sex, sex with a toy, penile–vaginal sex, and penile–anal sex) in a diverse cohort of United States adolescents. Data are from the QuaranTeen Health study, an online cohort study of adolescents aged 13–17 years. Participants reported the age they first engaged in each of the five behaviors or indicated no engagement on 5 follow-up surveys over 24 months. Our analytic sample included participants who reported no engagement in all five sexual behaviors at baseline ( N = 924). Among initiators ( N = 267, 29%), the most frequently reported first behavior(s) were fingering, oral, and penile–vaginal sex occurring during a single observation interval (22.8%), fingering and oral sex occurring during a single observation interval (18.7%), fingering alone (17.5%), and oral sex alone (10.4%). By 24 months, 33% of participants still under observation had engaged in fingering or oral sex and 25% had engaged in penile–vaginal sex. Sex with toys and penile–anal sex were less frequently reported and often paired with other behaviors. Most participants who initiated behavior(s) reported a first activity or combination at one observation and did not add additional behaviors under observation. Overall, while penile–vaginal sex was a frequently reported first sexual activity in our sample, fingering and oral sex were also common. Efforts to understand and support adolescent sexual development should consider a full range of sexual behaviors.

title: Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
A probabilistic region-based model for evaluating the integrated hosting capacity of photovoltaics and electric vehicles in power distribution networks
A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Real-time control of sustainable data centers: A two-layer model predictive control framework with workload flexibility and heat recovery
abstract: This paper proposes a two-layer model predictive control (MPC) framework for the real-time operation of data centers integrated with on-site photovoltaic generation, battery energy storage, waste heat recovery, and district heating. The upper layer employs scenario-based stochastic optimization to jointly optimize intraday market participation, workload scheduling, and energy management under uncertainty. The lower layer adopts an adaptive tube-based MPC strategy that compensates for short-term disturbances while tracking the dispatch references given by the upper layer. The framework further integrates multi-horizon forecasting to support real-time decision-making. Microservice-based simulation studies under representative clear-sky, overcast, and oversupply operating conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework accurately tracks dispatch plans despite fast photovoltaic and workload fluctuations. Compared with single-layer control strategies, the adaptive lower-layer controller substantially reduces real-time dispatch deviations and the associated imbalance costs. In addition, the proposed framework naturally adapts to seasonal operating conditions and responds to carbon-aware operating signals, offering a practical approach for economically efficient, sustainable, and grid-supportive operation of future data centers.

title: Land transfer experience and disparity between WTA and WTP: Evidence from China
Aligning mitigation incentives across technologies under the Paris Agreement's Article 6.4 mechanism
abstract: This article examines the incentive structure of the Paris Agreement’s Article 6.4 mechanism and document systematic misalignment of incentives across mitigation technologies and regions. Using project-level data, we estimate levelized emissions reduction costs across a wide range of mitigation activities and analyze their distributions. A machine-learning clustering algorithm classifies projects into seven global cost clusters, from which we derive relative weights per unit of emissions reduction.Our analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity in mitigation costs across technologies and locations. Yet observed deployment and credit issuance patterns are poorly aligned with these differences. High-cost projects account for a disproportionate share of credits relative to lower-cost activities. Across renewable categories, higher-cost projects issue fewer credits, revealing persistent incentive asymmetries. Estimated relative weights differ sharply across clusters, indicating that emissions reductions from high-cost technologies warrant proportionally greater support. Results are robust across alternative specifications.The findings underscore the importance of accounting for both cost and geographic heterogeneity in the design of climate finance under Article 6.4. By providing a transparent, data-driven, and flexible weighting tool, the framework offers policymakers a practical instrument to improve incentive alignment, maintain technological and regional diversity, and strengthen the integrity and effectiveness of global carbon markets.

title: Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Thermal short-circuiting in enhanced geothermal systems: Mechanisms, field evidence and emerging mitigation technologies
Towards sustainable and circular power semiconductor switches: Methodologies, challenges, and potential solutions
Out of sight, out of mind: Informal used vehicle trade as a blind spot in EV transition governance
abstract: International trade in second-hand vehicles (SHVs) plays an important but poorly documented role in shaping vehicle fleets and the geography of waste streams. In North America, one of the largest SHV trade flows globally occurs from the United States to Mexico, much of which is not captured in official trade statistics due to its informal nature. This study quantifies these unobserved flows, demonstrating how informal SHV trade obscures regional fleet dynamics and material flows and, as electrification accelerates, redistributes economic value and environmental risk embedded in used EV batteries across borders. We develop a novel modeling framework that integrates original on-the-ground vehicle survey data with literature benchmarks and administrative records to estimate Mexico's informal SHV stock. These estimates are embedded in a US–Mexico stock turnover model to reconstruct historical flows and project future dynamics. Results indicate that formal and informal SHV exports represent approximately 12–15% of annual US vehicle retirements but account for nearly 49% of vehicles entering the Mexican fleet, representing up to 70% of new vehicle additions in some states, concentrated in lower-income communities. Downstream, nearly 30% of cumulative US EOL EV battery mass may leave the country embedded in exported vehicles by 2050, while informal SHV imports are estimated to add an otherwise unaccounted 24–45% to vehicle retirements in Mexico. Policy interventions targeting upstream markets, particularly salvage vehicle auctions, could improve transparency and support more effective governance of the global EV transition, with implications for other regions, including the EU and China, where similar dynamics are emerging.

Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Thalassiosira pseudonana to Coated ZnO Nanoparticles and Their Mixtures under Long-Term, Low-Dose Exposure: The Dominant Role of Dissolved Zinc
abstract: Abstract The escalating production of engineered nanomaterials has raised concerns about their environmental impact. However, conventional short-term, high-dose ecotoxicity studies inadequately reflect realistic exposure scenarios. This study evaluated the long-term, low-dose toxicity of bare zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) and four representative silane-modified ZnO-NPs in the marine diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana. Algal cells were exposed for 14 days to individual ZnO-NPs, their binary mixtures (0.001–1 mg/L) or equimolar Zn2+ (0.0008–0.8 mg/L). Physiological and transcriptomic responses showed dose- and time-dependent toxicity, with largely comparable effects across nanoparticle and Zn2+ treatments. Growth inhibition by all zinc forms peaked at 38.0% within 0.01–0.1 mg/L and exceeded 90.0% at 1 mg/L, accompanied by reduced photosynthetic performance, altered chlorophyll a content, and elevated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptomic profiles of all ZnO-NPs resembled those of Zn2+, particularly for photosynthesis- and oxidative stress-related pathways. These similar responses were likely attributable to the substantial dissolution of all nanoparticles and their mixtures (44.3–89.2%), resulting in comparable cellular zinc bioaccumulation and Zn2+-like toxicity. Together, these findings reflect that the tested ZnO-NPs, whether silane-modified or present in mixtures, may behave similarly to dissolved zinc under chronic, environmentally relevant concentrations, highlighting the importance of incorporating such scenarios into ecological risk assessments of soluble metal-based nanomaterials.

title: Quantifying the Contribution of Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Amines to Nitrogenous Disinfection Byproduct Formation in Wastewater by Chemical Derivatization
abstract: Abstract Disinfection of wastewater effluent during water reuse produces nitrogenous disinfection byproducts (N-DBPs), many of which are more toxic than regulated DBPs. Despite progress in understanding N-DBP formation pathways from model compounds, the precursors of N-DBPs in authentic wastewater effluent remain largely unknown. Using derivatization reactions adapted from the synthetic organic chemistry literature, this study quantified the contribution of 1°, 2°, and 3° amines to the formation of three commonly studied N-DBP classes in wastewater effluent: N-nitrosamines, nitroalkanes, and haloacetonitriles. Derivatization reactions were first adapted to mild reaction conditions, and then derivatization effectiveness at suppressing N-DBP formation was assessed with known N-DBP precursors. Effluent organic matter was similarly derivatized to selectively block 1°, 1° and 2°, or all amines, and N-DBP formation after disinfection was compared to nonderivatized controls. NDMA formation was primarily attributable to secondary amines; nitromethane formation was attributable to primary amines, with secondary amines sometimes contributing significantly; and haloacetonitrile precursors varied by source, chiefly primary amines in two wastewaters, but secondary amines in another. Irrespective of amine order (1°/2°/3°), amines collectively comprised the majority of the N-DBP precursor pool, suggesting that insights from N-DBP formation mechanism studies using amines as model precursors are likely applicable to real wastewater.

title: Toxicity-Weighted Assessment Reveals the Rising Dominance of Non-Exhaust PM2.5 from On-Road Transportation in China
abstract: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emitted from nonexhaust sources, here defined as brake and tire wear, is attracting attention as vehicle exhaust emissions decline due to advanced aftertreatment devices and rapid fleet electrification. However, the relative toxicity of nonexhaust PM2.5 compared with tailpipe emissions remains insufficiently quantified under a unified methodology. In this study, oxidative stress and cytotoxicity potencies of nonexhaust PM2.5 are 5- to 11-fold higher than those of exhaust PM2.5 via dynamometer tests, chemical analyses, and in vitro cellular assays. By integrating these toxic potencies with compiled emission inventories and modeling, toxicity-adjusted emissions of nonexhaust PM2.5 in 2023 expanded to nearly eight times those of exhaust PM2.5 in China. Exposure hotspots were disproportionately concentrated in economically developed regions with dense traffic. Projections forecast the nonexhaust proportion in toxicity-adjusted on-road emissions to surge from 54% in 2014 to an overwhelming 96% by 2050. While fleet electrification eliminates tailpipe exhaust and regenerative braking reduces brake wear, the nonexhaust PM2.5 proportion will keep rising in the absence of dedicated control measures. Our findings underscore an urgent imperative to incorporate nonexhaust sources into future air quality management, prioritizing eco-friendly material innovations and establishing standardized regulatory metrics to safeguard public health.

title: Mind the Leak: Challenges of Riverbank Filtration for Highly Mobile Chemical Pollutants
abstract: Abstract Riverbank filtration (RBF) serves as a natural protective barrier for groundwater and drinking water sources. Growing evidence indicates that RBF is minimally effective at removing persistent, mobile, and toxic (PMT) substances, as well as very persistent and very mobile (vPvM) substances, which have recently been established as new hazard classes in the European Union. Owing to their resistance to biodegradation and sorption, these chemicals, including many pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals, can bypass wastewater treatment and natural riverbank barriers, ultimately contaminating groundwater and abstraction wells for drinking water. Current data gaps as well as analytical challenges hinder identification of PMT/vPvM substances in riverbank filtrate. One major data gap is that many of these substances are transformation products, some of which are formed by riverbank transformation processes. Varying geochemical and transient flow conditions further complicate prediction of the transport and fate of PMT substances, and the evolution of water quality, within RBF systems. To address these challenges, this Perspective proposes a progressive management strategy that integrates source reduction, reactive transport simulations, and nontargeted monitoring, as well as advanced multibarrier treatment, aimed at preventing and mitigating risks from PMT/vPvM substances in RBF systems.

title: Forensic Accounting of Kelp Carbon Sequestration: Geomorphic and Microbial Controls on Permanence and Verifiability
abstract: Abstract Kelp forests fix substantial amounts of carbon, but the fraction reaching long-term storage remains unclear. This review uses forensic accounting to assess evidence for kelp carbon sequestration, focusing on geomorphic and microbial controls on permanence and verifiability. Studies show kelp production and export, while retention estimates depend on the receiving environment and assessment period. Kelp-derived particulate carbon has been detected in deep water and sediments, whereas the long-term fate of kelp-derived dissolved organic carbon (DOC) remains poorly quantified. Geomorphology affects transport distance, source–sink connectivity, and access to depositional environments. Microbial processing controls degradation and remineralization and can generate recalcitrant DOC through the microbial carbon pump (MCP). Short transport pathways and slower degradation can increase particulate delivery, but retention also depends on circulation, ventilation, and postdepositional loss. For carbon remineralized to dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), storage duration depends on remineralization depth and water-mass ventilation. Persistent DOC storage estimates require source attribution, pool size, and residence time. We link each carbon claim to measurements in the receiving reservoir and distinguish marine carbon storage from net atmospheric CO2 removal and project-level crediting. Integrating source attribution, transport, microbial transformation, and reservoir retention can improve storage estimates and guide monitoring.

title: Dust Storms as Dynamic Multipollutant Exposure Systems: Environmental Transformation, Toxicological Mechanisms, and Health Implications
abstract: Abstract Dust particles have long been considered to be naturally derived mineral particles. However, with the increase in regional anthropogenic emissions and atmospheric multipollutant processes, their environmental significance as pollutant carriers and multicomponent exposure media has increasingly attracted attention. Nevertheless, existing studies have primarily focused on dust event characteristics, variations in particulate matter concentrations, or the effects of individual pollutant components, while a systematic understanding of the formation processes and health implications of dust as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system remains limited. This review conceptualizes dust storms as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system and integrates evidence from environmental chemistry, exposure science, toxicology, and epidemiology to discuss the environmental behavior of dust-associated pollutant components, their potential mechanisms of action, and their associations with population health effects. This review aims to advance the understanding of the processes underlying health risks associated with dust storms and provide a scientific basis for the development of future dust-related health risk assessment frameworks.

title: Can Small Modular Reactors Enable State-Specific Energy Portfolios for US AI Ambitions through 2035?
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of AI infrastructure in the US is emerging as a major new source of electricity demand, raising concerns about fossil lock-in during accelerated grid expansion. Here, we assess the role of small modular reactors (SMRs) within portfolios that also include on-site solar and wind power, grid electricity, battery storage, and direct air capture. Using a state-resolved scenario analysis for 2028–2035, we compare nuclear-inclusive and non-nuclear portfolios across alternative AI load trajectories, SSP-RCP electricity mixes, and decarbonization constraints. Relative to a grid-only counterfactual, nuclear-inclusive portfolios that achieve carbon neutrality by 2035 require 2.4–47.2 GW of SMR capacity, avoid 0.3–1.3 GtCO2, reduce water consumption by an amount equivalent to the annual use of 28.3–50.5 million people, and deliver \$105.8–194.8 billion in cumulative energy-system cost savings across climate and efficiency pathways. The results show that SMRs can materially expand cost-effective decarbonization options for AI infrastructure, while their contribution depends on timely deployment, permitting, and coordination with state-level electricity planning.

title: Internal Molecular Response Chains to Inhaled Volatile Organic Compounds for Precision Health Risk Assessment Revealed by Breathomics
abstract: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are airborne pollutants, yet risk assessment based solely on external concentrations may miss internal molecular effects under low-level mixture exposure. We collected exhaled breath and ambient air samples from 67 child volunteers for VOC profiling, with blood samples from 16 participants used for transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. A physiological compartment-based kinetic model identified 76 endogenous and 44 exogenous VOCs in breath, and dimensionality reduction grouped exogenous VOCs into seven chemically interpretable exposure patterns. These patterns were associated with 86 genes involving cell cycle and neural pathways and nominally with 247 metabolites, suggesting potential variation in energy, lipid and amino acid metabolism, and neurotransmitter homeostasis. Multiomics integration further suggested seven endogenous VOCs as candidate signals reflecting variation across exposure, transcriptome, and metabolome layers. Benzothiazole, 3,7-dimethyl-nonane, and 2-methyl-2-propenoic acid were associated with both conventional cancer risk estimates and cancer pathway activity, whereas conventional cancer risk showed only weak correlation with this internal phenotype. These findings support an internal molecular response framework connecting inhaled VOC exposure to biological effects and highlight the potential of breathomics for precision health risk assessment.

title: Air–Water Interfacial Secondary Hydroxylation of SO2: An Overlooked and Rapid Pathway to Sulfuric Acid in Tropical Coastal Industrial Areas
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is a key driver of acid deposition, aerosol growth, and new particle formation. Its formation is initiated by rapid OH addition to SO2 to produce HOSO2, but direct hydroxylation of HOSO2 is kinetically unfavorable. Consequently, the accepted route to H2SO4 proceeds via O2 oxidation of HOSO2 to SO3, followed by hydrolysis. Here, using classical molecular dynamics (MD) and Born–Oppenheimer MD simulations, we identify an alternative interfacial pathway that directly converts HOSO2 and OH into H2SO4. Strong interfacial affinity of both reactants drives this transformation at the air–water interface with a free-energy barrier of only 1.73 kcal·mol–1, substantially lower than that of gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis. Kinetic analysis further indicates that, under conditions of elevated OH, HOSO2, and low SO3, this pathway can outpace gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis by more than 3 orders of magnitude. These results reveal an efficient interfacial source of atmospheric H2SO4, offering a mechanistic basis for its elevated abundance in polluted coastal environments and improving the representation of sulfur oxidation in atmospheric models.

title: Environmentally Relevant F-53B Exposure Triggers Ovarian Cancer Progression via C5aR1-Mediated Noncanonical Signaling: An Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) Underlying Hybrid EMT and Stemness
abstract: Significant gaps remain in the health risk assessment methodologies for the PFOS (perfluorooctanesulfonic acid) alternative 6:2 Cl-PFESA (6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate, F-53B), which has been widely recognized as the alternative to PFOS in China. To address this research gap, our study integrated multidimensional techniques to mechanistically construct an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for F-53B-induced ovarian cancer progression. Our findings demonstrated that exposure to environmentally relevant concentrations of F-53B significantly enhanced the migratory and invasive capabilities of ovarian cancer cells. Within the AOP framework of F-53B-induced hybrid epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and enhanced tumor stemness, the upregulation of C5aR1─triggered by ERα acting as a noncanonical receptor of F-53B─constitutes the molecular initiating event (MIE). Following this MIE, the recruitment of β-arrestin1 and Src was induced, leading to the assembly of a C5aR1/β-arrestin1/Src signaling complex. This complex facilitated the binding of β-arrestin1 to β-catenin and drove the nuclear translocation of β-catenin, ultimately activating hybrid EMT and stemness of tumor cells. Administration of the C5aR1 inhibitor PMX205 effectively abrogated subsequent key events (KEs) caused by F-53B exposure. Through in vitro and in vivo validation, our study established an AOP framework that provides a novel perspective for evaluating the potential risk of PFAS substitutes in promoting cancer progression.

title: Landfills Act as Persistent Reservoirs of Rubber-Derived Chemicals, Driving Widespread Subsurface Migration and Groundwater Contamination
abstract: Abstract Rubber-derived chemicals (RDCs) are emerging contaminants of concern in various environments, yet their occurrence, migration, and ecological risks in landfill and groundwater remain insufficiently understood. In this study, 35 RDCs were investigated in landfill leachate and groundwater from three municipal landfills, covering raw and treated leachate as well as upstream, on-site, and downstream groundwater across wet and dry seasons. Results showed widespread detection of RDCs in all matrices, with benzothiazoles and other RDCs reaching peak levels of 85890 ng/L, substantially exceeding p-phenylenediamines (PPDs, 869 ng/L) and their quinones (PPD-Qs, 443 ng/L). Although conventional treatment reduced total RDC levels, most compounds remained detectable in effluents (1.10–4946 ng/L). Groundwater analyses revealed clear spatial gradients, with on-site aquifers showing the highest contamination, while downstream groundwater still exhibited significantly elevated concentrations and compositional similarity to landfill leachate, implying subsurface migration. Seasonal variation was observed only in on-site groundwater, indicating that landfill systems amplify climatic effects on contaminant behavior. Risk assessment further indicated that PPD-Qs and 1,3-diphenylguanidine (DPG) were primary contributors to ecological risk in both leachate and groundwater (RQ far above 1). Overall, landfill systems act as persistent sources and subsurface conduits of RDCs, posing long-term risks to surrounding groundwater environments.

title: Broad Nuclear Receptor-Binding Activities of Phase II Sulfate Metabolites Revealed by the Combinatorial Synthesis for Environmental Research (CoSyER) Approach with Affinity Selection Mass Spectrometry (ASMS)
abstract: Abstract Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput combinatorial synthesis for environmental research and a protein affinity selection mass spectrometry approach (CoSyER:ASMS) for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks. As proof of concept, 132 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach. Four nuclear receptors (PPARγ, PXR, ERRγ, and FXR) were further selected for AS-MS analysis to evaluate the binding activities of 132 sulfate metabolites and corresponding parent compounds, covering 1056 binary interactions. Interestingly, sulfate metabolites exhibited broad nuclear receptor-binding activities toward PPARγ and PXR, with 29 and 24 ligands detected by AS-MS, respectively. Bioactivities and functional effects of triclosan sulfate and 1-hydroxypyrene sulfate were validated by orthogonal fluorescence assay and human cell receptor assays. Collectively, this study introduces CoSyER:ASMS as a scalable platform integrating high-throughput generation of sulfate metabolites with receptor-binding screening to accelerate the toxicological prioritization of this understudied metabolite class.

title: Screening Environmental Toxicants for Neurodevelopmental Disorders Using a hPSC-Based Mitochondrial Redox Biosensor
abstract: Abstract Environmental chemical exposure during prenatal development significantly elevates the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), with mitochondrial oxidative stress representing a central convergent mechanism. However, existing screening platforms lack the genetic stability and developmental stage specificity required for systematic identification of neurotoxic hazards across human neural lineage progression. Here, we established a human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-based mitochondrial redox biosensor by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted integration of the genetically encoded H2O2 probe mito-HyPer7 into the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus, ensuring stable expression across pluripotent, neurogenic, and neuronal stages. Using this platform, we screened 76 epidemiologically relevant industrial chemicals and identified reactive oxygen species-inducing toxicants (ROS-ITs) with lineage-stage-selective profiles across neural lineages. Neural progenitor cells (NPCs) exhibited the broadest sensitivity spectrum, revealing neurogenesis as a critical developmental window. Among the screened compounds, bisphenol G (BPG)─an emerging alternative in plastic production─displayed cross-stage toxicity surpassing that of bisphenol A (BPA). In three-dimensional cortical organoids, BPG impaired radial glial cell (RGC) proliferation, triggered precocious neurogenic transition, and induced apoptosis, culminating in disrupted cortical architecture. Mechanistically, BPG aberrantly activated thyroid hormone receptor (TR)-mediated transcription, and the resulting developmental impairment was partially ameliorated by the receptor antagonist NH-3. Collectively, this study presents an integrative framework that unites a genetically stable platform for high-throughput mitochondrial redox screening with organoid-based pathological and mechanistic validation, providing a comprehensive paradigm for identifying and characterizing environmental toxicants that threaten human neurodevelopment.

title: Continuous and Episodic Metal Exposures Disrupt Aquatic Insect Drift, Emergence, and Larval Survival
abstract: Abstract Metal contamination in streams occurs under both chronic and episodic exposures, yet the effects of varying exposure on invertebrate life-history processes are poorly understood. We conducted two 9-day mesocosm experiments with benthic macroinvertebrate communities to compare the effects of continuous and pulsed exposures to dissolved copper and zinc on larval drift, adult emergence, and benthic survival. Our goal was to evaluate how different exposure regimes alter in situ survival relative to the downstream movement of invertebrate prey resources and their dispersal to terrestrial consumers. Both exposure regimes significantly increased total larval drift (29–52% above controls), with Baetidae (Ephemeroptera) and Hydropsychidae (Trichoptera) dominating the drift response. Cumulative daily drift increased rapidly after initial exposure, with Baetidae under continuous exposure showing 3-fold higher drift relative to controls. Total emergence was higher under continuous exposure and was primarily driven by stimulated emergence in Chironomidae (Diptera). Total benthic abundance declined by 24–33% across treatments and was similar between exposure regimes, suggesting responses were more strongly associated with peak concentrations than cumulative dose. Together, our results show that continuous and episodic metal exposures can reduce benthic abundance while simultaneously increasing emigration through drift and emergence, thereby altering critical ecosystem services provided by aquatic insects.

Crisis as catalyst: Board composition and ESG controversies in crisis conditions
abstract: Environmental, social and governance (ESG) controversies are discrete, incident-based events with reputational and financial consequences that aggregate ESG scores overlook. We examine whether board gender diversity, board tenure and board-specific skills are associated with firms’ exposure to such controversies, and whether these associations differ between stable and crisis periods. Using a balanced panel of 386 S&P 500 firms for 2017–2022 and the LSEG (formerly Refinitiv) ESG Controversies Score, where higher values mean fewer controversies, we interact each board attribute with a post-COVID indicator in two-way fixed-effects models and test the post-COVID associations directly. The within-firm association between board gender diversity and the controversy score becomes significantly more positive after 2020, with no sign of change in earlier years. The shift is robust to sample trimming, alternative samples, control sets and inference procedures, but weakens when board characteristics are lagged. The post-COVID association itself is positive but not statistically distinguishable from zero. Board tenure and board-specific skills show no significant association in either period and no robust change, and dynamic panel estimates are too weakly identified to be informative. The evidence is associational: the relation between gender diversity and controversy exposure changed when stakeholder scrutiny intensified, consistent with a crisis-contingent resource dependence account, but more diverse boards cannot be shown to have reduced controversies, and changes in media attention, disclosure and economic conditions may have contributed. For large listed firms under intensive ESG scrutiny, board evidence from stable periods may not carry over to crises.

Rethinking environmental justice through behavioural opportunity: developing a relational territorial vulnerability framework from IPSA-derived behavioural evidence
abstract: Environmental justice research has primarily explained health inequalities through environmental risks and resource distribution. Public spaces have similarly been assessed through quantity and accessibility, with planning interventions focused on optimizing resource allocation. However, this provision-oriented paradigm overlooks the behavioural dimension of spatial equity: health benefits depend on whether residents can translate public-space resources into stable, sufficient, and demand-responsive opportunities for health-supportive everyday activities. This limitation is particularly pressing in high-density cities, where spatial competition and socioeconomic inequality complicate the relationship between formal provision and actual use. We therefore reconsider environmental justice through the lens of behavioural opportunity. Drawing on theories of everyday public life and environmental affordance, we define Informal Public Space Activities (IPSAs) as self-initiated, stationary recreational, social, or physical practices occurring without formal programming or purpose-built facilities. Long-term IPSA observations reveal mismatches between residents' behavioural demands and existing public-space support conditions, identifying latent opportunity deficits that remain overlooked in conventional planning approaches. Based on that, vulnerability is reconceptualized as a relational condition arising from interactions between environmental risks and residents' behavioural demands, rather than from environmental exposure or demographic characteristics alone. Methodologically, this study introduces IPSA-derived behavioural opportunity inequalities into a city-scale territorial vulnerability assessment framework. We use Ward and Jaccard methods to identify territorial clusters with different environmental burdens and behavioural opportunity deficits in Hong Kong, a high-density case. Findings show that although isolated hotspots of environmental deficiency exist, areas characterised by compounded environmental and social vulnerabilities more clearly reveal priority locations for behavioural-supportive spatial interventions. The framework introduces a behavioural opportunity perspective into environmental impact assessment, making concealed behavioural inequalities assessable and extending environmental justice from exposure equity to behavioural opportunity equity. It further demonstrates how future public-space projects can integrate environmental risk mitigation with behavioural support, enabling differentiated planning, design, and governance responses across distinct territorial vulnerability contexts.

title: Discursive social life cycle assessment: Performance assessment based on public evidence
abstract: This study introduces a framework that integrates Discourse Analysis (DA) into Social Life Cycle Assessment (Social LCA) to enhance the collection and interpretation of contextualized qualitative data. While Social LCA is instrumental for evaluating social impacts, it often lacks methodological depth regarding subjective and publicly available data. To bridge this gap, the methodology aligns the phases of Social LCA with the stages of DA specifically employing corpus selection to define the study's scope and DA to process social inventory data from public sources. A detailed procedural flow was developed, featuring impact categories, subcategories, and indicators derived from international guidelines, literature, and national legal regulations. The proposal utilizes a reference scale with scores ranging from “critical social violation” to “transformative ethical leadership” to classify social performance. By treating organizational discourse as material evidence and confronting it through source triangulation, corporate narratives are synthesized into systematic impact scores, aiming to enhance methodological consistency, traceability, and auditability through a standardized interpretive protocol. The study concludes that this integrated approach aims to contribute to the analytical rigor of Social LCA by enabling a critical analysis of corporate sustainability discourses compared to actual practices. This methodology allows for the identification of strategic silences, ideological masks, and social greenwashing. Ultimately, the framework seeks to provide consumers, regulators, and investors with analytical tools, potentially assisting the transition from passive recipients of information into critical subjects. This work advances the theoretical understanding of the relationship between discourse, power, and social impact within the corporate sustainability agenda.
authors: Italo Emmanoel Mesquita Oliveira de Moura

title: Governing the invisible: From reactive to proactive groundwater governance under water scarcity in Europe
abstract: Groundwater is central to Europe's water security, yet it faces increasing pressure from climate change, growing water demand, and unsustainable management. Besides drought triggering reactive responses, creeping water scarcity threatens to undermine Europe's water security and calls for proactive and anticipatory governance. Using a multi-level governance analysis framework, we draw on stakeholder interviews and document analysis to investigate groundwater governance across four European groundwater systems as case study sites; the Dommel in the Netherlands, the Dijle and Nete in Belgium, the Alfamén and Cariñena in Spain, and Kalmar in Sweden. The analysis identifies how governance competencies change under drought conditions, identifying institutional lock-ins, policy gaps, and the role of non-governmental actors in shaping adaptive capacity under conditions of water scarcity, particularly studying responses to drought events. The findings demonstrate that governance outcomes are often reactive, and only incrementally adapting to the growing threat due to institutional arrangements, historical development trajectories, and political-economic contexts. The paper in turn argues that strengthening groundwater governance from a water scarcity framework can enhance resilience by shifting from crisis response to proactive long-term management, addressing root/structural issues.

title: Soil Seed Bank and Aboveground Vegetation Relationships and Restoration Effects of Typical Sand‐Fixation Models in Mu Us Sandy Land
abstract: ABSTRACT To reveal the ecological restoration effects and intrinsic mechanisms of the artificial shrub mixed sand‐fixation model in the Mu Us Sandy Land. We selected four typical sand‐fixation models, namely Corethrodendron fruticosum and Juniperus sabina (Js), Corethrodendron fruticosum and Artemisia ordosica (Ao), Corethrodendron fruticosum and Salix cheilophila (Sc), and Corethrodendron fruticosum and Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica (Pa), as the research objects, with mobile sandy land as the control (CK). Through field investigation and sampling, laboratory germination experiments, and index determination, we systematically analyzed soil nutrients and enzyme activities, aboveground vegetation community structure, soil seed bank characteristics, and their correlations. All four sand‐fixation models significantly enhanced soil nitrate nitrogen (NO 3 − ‐N), ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 + ‐N) contents, and urease (UR) activity, with the Pa model achieving the best NO 3 − ‐N accumulation and the Js model the highest NH 4 + ‐N content. Nevertheless, in the early sand‐fixation stage, soil organic matter and the activities of cellulase, dehydrogenase, and other enzymes were lower than CK. Meanwhile, aboveground vegetation density increased significantly, with the Sc and Pa models showing outstanding performance, and the community succeeded to a perennial herb‐shrub mixed type. Notably, the Ao model had the highest soil seed bank density, and all seed banks exhibited surface‐enriched distribution. Soil NO 3 − ‐N, NH 4 + ‐N, and UR are closely linked to the regulation of vegetation and seed bank characteristics. The Sc pattern possessed the highest similarity coefficient (0.46) and showed the strongest coupling relationship between seed bank and aboveground vegetation. This research uncovers the variations in ecological effects of different sand‐fixation configurations, offering scientific support for optimizing sand‐fixation patterns and promoting ecological restoration in the Mu Us Sandy Land.

title: Navigating industrial diversification in megacities: interconnections between industrial dynamics and changing commuting patterns in Shanghai
abstract: Abstract Industrial diversification plays an essential role in the longer-term growth of urban economies. However, its effects on daily life are less explored. Using microdata on firms and mobility across 164 subdistricts of Shanghai, this study applies an evolutionary economic geography framework to assess how intra-urban industrial diversification influences commuting patterns. We find that diversification into more unrelated and complex industries increases commuting duration and distance, suggesting that while industrial diversification fosters economic growth, it may raise concerns about quality of life and social inequities. Possible moderating effects like employment density, transit access and housing supply are discussed.

title: Temporal tradeoffs and contracting dynamics in buyer–supplier agreements
abstract: Abstract Research Summary We examine temporal tradeoffs and contracting dynamics in buyer–supplier agreements by investigating how suppliers' contractual terms change when contracting with initial clients versus new clients in the future. We use information economics and research on certifications in interorganizational relationships to delve into the mechanisms leading to potential improvements in suppliers' contractual terms. We situate the empirical analysis in the context of onshore oil and gas drilling projects to examine the liabilities for project‐related risks that startup drillers assume when contracting with client producers. Evidence indicates that when drillers initially work for prominent client producers, the drillers assume more risks in these first contracts, but fewer risks in subsequent agreements with other client producers. We argue and show that the degree to which a specific driller obtains better terms in future deals owing to its initial client's prominence will be attenuated when subsequent clients have more information on the value of the driller's resources and capabilities. Specifically, the resulting reduction in risks borne by the driller will be smaller when the driller was founded by a serial entrepreneur and when the subsequent client is vertically integrated into drilling operations. Managerial Summary This study examines the contracting dynamics that startups experience as suppliers in buyer–supplier agreements. Startups often bear more risk in initial deals to build credibility, especially when contracting with prominent clients, and such affiliations can then lead to improved terms for startups in subsequent contracts with other clients. However, this follow‐on benefit of working with a prominent client depends upon whether subsequent clients have more information on the startup's resources and capabilities. In particular, the risk‐reduction effect of working with an initial client that is prominent will be smaller for those startups founded by serial entrepreneurs. It will also be smaller when the subsequent client is vertically integrated into the value chain activities carried out by the startup. Using data from startups in the oil and gas drilling industry, we illustrate the dynamics and tradeoffs that startup drillers encounter when contracting with established client producers.

title: Interorganizational Accounting: The Role of BRSR in Driving Accountability of Pharmaceutical Supply Chain
abstract: ABSTRACT Pharmaceutical supply chains are significant players contributing to the economy of a nation. This has resulted in widespread pollution of the environment, harming both human health and the ecosystem. This study examines the business responsibility and sustainability reporting (BRSR) disclosures of 59 Indian pharmaceutical businesses (ranked in the top 1000 by 2025). The research employs a systematic process that includes data extraction using automation tools and analysis with Python libraries. The examination looks at a variety of topics, including product focus, operational efficiency, environmental performance, employees' demographics, and stakeholder involvement. The findings demonstrate differences in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance among organizations. As the study is on pharmaceutical companies, it also examines the attributes embedded in Good Manufacturing Practices (a system of rules and guidelines). To explain the phenomenon, the authors integrated insights from the resource‐based view and institutional theory. This research study has integrated interpretive structural modelling with structural equation modelling to identify the good manufacturing practices (GMP) drivers and enablers. The study was conducted at two levels. In the first level, experts were interviewed to understand the interrelationship between drivers and BRSR practices. In the second level, an interpretive structural model was developed, and the identified relationships were tested using structural equation modelling. The results revealed that regulatory pressure and competition were the key drivers for good manufacturing practices. This research provides significant insights for investors, policymakers, and the pharmaceutical sector as a whole in navigating the complicated terrain of sustainability reporting and making meaningful progress towards ESG goals.

Cord-Blood Metal Mixtures and Birth Weight: Individual and Joint Associations in a Large German Cohort
abstract: Abstract Fetal circulating metal profiles may be associated with birth weight, but evidence from direct fetal biomonitoring remains limited. We measured 37 metals in cord whole blood from 1,085 singleton mother–infant pairs in Berlin and evaluated associations with birth weight using regression and mixture approaches. In mutually adjusted multimetal models, cobalt (Co) and strontium (Sr) were positively associated with birth weight, whereas copper (Cu) was inversely associated; none remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Elastic net regression retained no metals when covariates were unpenalized; Co, Sr, and Cu emerged as prominent contributors in exploratory jointly penalized analyses. Quantile g-computation indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in the Co–Cu–Sr mixture was associated with 48.07 g higher birth weight (95% CI: 7.13–89.02 g). Bayesian kernel machine regression and generalized additive models suggested interactions involving Co, with higher Co attenuating the inverse Cu association and strengthening the positive Sr association. Paired maternal and cord-blood measurements showed element-specific differences. These findings suggest associations between fetal metal profiles and birth weight, with exploratory mixture analyses indicating potential joint and interactive associations among Co, Cu, and Sr. Combining direct fetal biomonitoring with mixture analyses may improve assessment of fetal metal burden and health implications.

Across Three Orders of Magnitude From Local to Global Scales: The Influence of Climate on Soil Salinity Intensifies
abstract: ABSTRACT Soil salinity accumulation has become a widespread global phenomenon, adversely affecting land degradation, vegetation, crops, and human livelihoods. Identifying the dominant controlling factors of soil salinity across different scales is crucial for understanding land degradation and developing effective restoration strategies. To this end, this study utilized ECe (dS/m) measurements from 22,111 soil profiles in the WOSIS database, combined with data‐driven models, geo‐environmental factors, and multi‐scale analysis methods to reveal the environmental controls on soil salinity across three depth intervals at six spatial scales ranging from local to global. The study found that as sample size increased, the accuracy of multi‐scale salinity modeling gradually improved, particularly for subsurface soils (0.3–0.6 m) and at larger spatial scales (> 500 km), where additional samples significantly enhanced prediction accuracy. Based on the calibrated model, we found that extreme climate (extreme weather events due to climate change) dominates soil salinity (3.9%–40% importance) across spatial scales (25–2000 km). Extreme climate is also the primary controlling factor for soil salinity in nine biomes and at the global scale (24%–47% explanatory power). The nonlinear relationships between soil salinity and individual factors varied with depth and spatial scale; these relationships showed an initial increase/decrease to a specific threshold before stabilizing or reversing. This study reveals the dominant factors and nonlinear response patterns of soil salinity across multiple scales, providing critical theoretical foundations and decision‐making support for global salinization management.

title: Correction to “Environmental Governance, Urban Sustainability, and Adaptation Strategies: The Nexus of Food–Water–Energy”
Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

title: Molecular adhesion for durable metal halide perovskite modules
abstract: Reliable, strong, and low-loss interfaces are needed for durable perovskite photovoltaics. We have developed a molecular interface layer with an aromatic dual-site-binding ligand to improve the reliability of perovskite modules. The buried interface was strengthened through intermolecular interactions between the ligand and hole-selective layer and through strong chemical bonds. The resulting heterointerface enhances perovskite adhesion and releases interface strain, making the device more resilient to thermomechanical stresses. This device architecture achieves a power conversion efficiency of 22.7% for 900–square centimeter (cm 2 ) submodules (aperture area: 655 cm 2 ) and 21.3% for 7200-cm 2 standard modules (aperture area: 6380 cm 2 ). The champion 7200-cm 2 standard module maintained consistent performance during 105 days of outdoor testing, as independently measured by the Photovoltaic Accelerator for Commercializing Technologies (PACT) center.

title: Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.

title: Elastic-field reorganization stabilizes soft-lattice perovskites for durable solar cells
abstract: The soft lattice that enables the exceptional performance of halide perovskites inherently compromises their operational stability. Here, we show that soft-lattice perovskites can be stabilized through elastic-field reorganization induced by rigid nanodiamond inclusions. Their inclusion enabled efficient bulk-to-boundary load transfer, redistributing and dissipating internal elastic fields at grain boundaries rather than allowing their accumulation within the crystal interior. Suppression of intergranular sliding constrained lattice deformation and mitigated defect generation during prolonged operation. Devices based on the stabilized perovskites with an area of 0.09 square centimeters achieved a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.6%, and minimodules with an area of 16.1 square centimeters achieved 24.3%. These devices retained 80% of their initial PCE after 5000 hours of maximum power point operation at 85°C and 98% after 5000 hours of dynamically varying light-intensity day-night cycling.

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

title: The scientific record is never finished
abstract: The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

title: The fate of poised pre-mRNAs shapes mitochondrial activity and cellular differentiation
abstract: Although RNA quality control tightly regulates gene expression, the scope of its regulatory functions in the nucleus remains unclear. In this study, we describe the quality control, on chromatin, of poised intron–containing polyadenylated RNAs (PIA-RNAs). Whether these precursor messenger RNAs (pre-mRNAs) constitute immature mRNAs whose splicing is pending or, alternatively, are degraded by the nuclear RNA exosome depends on whether they engage nuclear cap-binding protein 3 (NCBP3) or anillin, respectively. Many PIA-RNAs inversely controlled by NCBP3 and anillin encode mitochondrial factors. Thus, NCBP3 depletion in mouse as well as pathogenic mutations in the RNA exosome in humans result in reduced mitochondrial activity, muscle weakness, cerebellar hypomyelination, and diminished motor coordination. Our findings reveal a competition between pre-mRNA metabolic pathways whose balance controls mitochondrial function and, when perturbed, leads to neurological diseases.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: Divergent activation of the RXFP1 relaxin receptor by protein and small-molecule agonists
abstract: The relaxin receptor RXFP1 is a therapeutic target owing to its potential benefits in the treatment of fibrosis and heart failure. Protein and small-molecule agonists are currently in midstage clinical trials for various forms of heart disease. In this work, we present three cryo–electron microscopy structures of RXFP1: ligand-free, bound to the native agonist relaxin-2, and bound to the small-molecule drug candidate AZD5462. These structures reveal that relaxin-2 engages the receptor’s ectodomain, whereas AZD5462 binds to the transmembrane domain. Together with hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, we show that relaxin-2 induces reorganization of the linker domain into a helical secondary structure. By contrast, AZD5462 stabilizes an active conformation through a distinct set of conformational rearrangements. Altogether, our findings define divergent activation mechanisms for protein and small-molecule agonists of RXFP1.

title: Save scientific terminology from executive orders
Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40 Ca + . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

title: Making ecological programs work at scale
Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

title: Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

Market Response to Racial Uprisings
abstract: Do investors anticipate that demands for racial equity will impact companies? We explore this question in the context of the Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement—the largest racially motivated protest movement in U.S. history—and its effect on the U.S. policing industry using a novel dataset on publicly traded firms contracting with the police. It is unclear whether the BLM uprisings were likely to increase or decrease market valuations of firms contracting heavily with police because of the increased interest in reforming the police, fears over rising crime, and pushes to “defund the police”. We find, in contrast to the predictions of economics experts we surveyed, that in the three weeks following incidents triggering BLM uprisings, policing firms experienced a stock price increase of seven percentage points relative to the stock prices of nonpolicing firms in similar industries. In particular, firms producing surveillance technology and police accountability tools experienced higher returns following BLM activism–related events. Furthermore, policing firms’ fundamentals, such as sales, improved after the murder of George Floyd, suggesting that policing firms’ future performances bore out investors' positive expectations following incidents triggering BLM uprisings. Our research shows how—despite BLM’s calls to reduce investment in policing and explore alternative public safety approaches—the financial market has translated high-profile violence against Black civilians and calls for systemic change into shareholder gains and additional revenues for police suppliers.

title: Intermediate Input Prices and the Labor Share
abstract: We argue that the relative price of materials is an important determinant of the labor share of income. When materials and primary inputs are complements and the profit share is positive, a higher price of materials lowers the labor share and raises the profit share of value added, without requiring markups or returns to scale to change. We show that materials-price fluctuations align with U.S. labor-share trends, provide causal evidence on this mechanism across industries and commuting zones, and quantify its importance in a dynamic quantitative model. Finally, we use our mechanism to rationalize differential labor-share trends across countries. Institutional subscribers to the NBER working paper series, and residents of developing countries may download this paper without additional charge at www.nber.org.

title: Unemployment Benefits and Unemployment in the Great Recession: The Role of Equilibrium Effects
abstract: Equilibrium labor market theory suggests that unemployment benefit extensions affect unemployment by impacting both job search decisions by the unemployed and job creation decisions by employers. The existing empirical literature focused on the former effect only. We develop a new methodology necessary to incorporate the measurement of the latter effect. Implementing this methodology in the data, we find that benefit extensions raise equilibrium wages and lead to a sharp contraction in vacancy creation and employment and a rise in unemployment.

title: Prospect Theory and Currency Returns: Empirical Evidence
abstract: We empirically investigate the role of prospect theory in the foreign exchange market. A currency-level measure of prospect-theory value, constructed from the historical distribution of exchange rate returns, negatively forecasts future currency excess returns. A long–short strategy based on this measure yields approximately 5% per annum. Predictability is stronger when arbitrage is limited. Bank order flow is positively associated with prospect-theory value, with inter-dealer and proprietary trading primarily driving this relation. Funds trade against prospect-theory value, acting as arbitrageurs. Overall, our findings suggest that investors evaluate currencies based on historical return distributions, consistent with prospect theory.
journal_name: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis

title: Trended Momentum
abstract: Drawing on cognitive psychology and behavioral theories of pattern recognition and heuristic processing, we offer a new perspective on momentum by highlighting how clear price trends shape investor expectations. Trend clarity (TC) materially strengthens momentum returns: the highest trend-clarity quintile earns annualized returns of 12.68%, compared with 6.90% for a conventional momentum strategy. We also show that TC affects momentum trading intensity within Hong and Stein’s (1999) multiperiod return-chasing model. Additional tests indicate that trading on clear trends is a central feature of momentum, distinct from existing explanations and observable across asset classes and global markets.
